title: Tenant weekly snapshot hydration and dimension affinity curation
creator: Avery Lin
description:
Summary:
Create a curated, compact weekly snapshot table for tenant-level Console usage that pre-hydrates key dimensions (routes, models, workspace metadata, billing tier) and encodes affinity signals for fast, low-cost ad-hoc queries and dashboard/alert consumption. This ticket covers schema design, ingestion pipeline, compaction/retention strategy, and rollout to prod-staging-console schema. Goal is sub-second dashboard queries for common slices and >10x reduction in downstream join costs for Console dashboards and SLA/cost attribution jobs.

Motivation & goals:
- Many Console dashboards and quick-look APIs currently run multi-join queries across raw invocation facts, route metadata, and tenant entitlements. These are expensive and sensitive to cardinality spikes.
- Provide a denormalized weekly snapshot (tenant_weekly_usage_v1) pre-joined with canonical dimensions, with encoded affinity tags for route/model co-occurrence and feature exposures (eg. streaming, embeddings, reranking).
- Support both streaming incremental updates (nearline) and a compact weekly snapshot materialization for fast analytics.

Design decisions (summary):
- Table shape: moderately wide, columnar Parquet in Snowflake external stage + materialized micro-partitioned Snowflake table. Partition by week_start_date and tenant_id; cluster on route_id and model_family to speed common predicates.
- Column strategy: keep high-cardinality fields as encoded enums/ids, store affinity_signatures as VARIANT (JSON string) with a deterministic bucketed fingerprint to limit cardinality. Avoid free-form text in the snapshot.
- Denorm vs star: choose denormalized snapshot for common Console queries (trade-off: larger storage vs order-of-magnitude faster queries). Keep a lightweight dimension store (canonical_route, canonical_model, tenant_profile) for backfills and edge lookups.
- Late-arrival handling: streaming input uses an event-time watermark of 2 days and writes to a nearline staging table; weekly compaction job reconciles late data with a deterministic update strategy (upsert by (tenant_id, week_start, route_id)).
- Backfill strategy: rolling backfills in 2-week windows to avoid huge single jobs; use Spark job with date range partitioning and snapshot diff checksums.

Ingestion & pipeline:
- Nearline: Flink->Kafka topic -> Spark Structured Streaming job produces tenant_weekly_usage_nearline (hourly micro-batches) in raw micro-partitioned format.
- Compaction: Airflow DAG runs weekly to fold nearline into tenant_weekly_usage_v1 (upsert), creates compact delta file set, and executes VACUUM/retention.
- Metrics & SLOs: target compaction job latency < 4 hours after week close; snapshot query 95th percentile < 800ms for common Console API slices.

Schema (highlight):
- tenant_id STRING, week_start_date DATE, total_invocations BIGINT, successful_invocations BIGINT, avg_latency_ms DOUBLE, token_cost_estimate DOUBLE, unique_routes INT, top_routes ARRAY<STRING>, affinity_signature STRING, model_family STRING, billing_tier STRING, features_applied ARRAY<STRING>, footprint_mb DOUBLE, snapshot_ts TIMESTAMP
- NOTE: affinity_signature is a deterministic 64-bit hex fingerprint of a normalized vector of route+model co-occurrence buckets. This keeps cardinality bounded while preserving grouping power for cohort queries.

Trade-offs considered:
- Wide snapshot increases storage by ~20-30% but eliminates dozens of joins and temp-table scans for dashboards. Estimated incremental storage for all tenants: ~18TB/year (compressed).
- Alternative of precomputed rollups by route x tenant would explode cardinality; we opted for a single tenant-week snapshot with encoded vectors.

Rolling plan & rollout checklist:
- [x] Design doc on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/tenant-weekly-snapshot (initial draft)
- [x] Schema review with Analytics (2026-02-20) — resolved cardinality concerns by adding fingerprinting
- [x] PoC: small-tenant backfill and query comparison (PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/data-pipelines/pull/459)
- [x] Unit tests for fingerprinting & deterministic upsert (CI: pipelines/build/459)
- [ ] Integration tests in staging: validate backfill parity and cost regression (blocked by staging Snowflake slot availability)
- [ ] Security review (requested 2026-03-01) — pending data governance sign-off
- [ ] Run staggered prod backfill for last 8 weeks (low priority tenants first)
- [ ] Enable Console dashboards to point to new snapshot table via views and retire old heavy queries

Progress notes / timeline: 
- 2026-02-15: Ticket opened. Initial scoping meeting with PM (Samantha Ortiz) and Analytics (Priya Nair).
- 2026-02-18: Benchmarked single-week backfill on medium-size tenant; snapshot query improved median runtime from 6s->0.42s for common filters. Recorded in experiment notes.
- 2026-02-20: Schema review; decided to implement fingerprinted affinity instead of high-cardinality route arrays.
- 2026-02-24: PoC backfill complete for 50 tenants; PR #459 created for pipeline code and tests.
- 2026-02-28: Observability hooks added (airflow metrics, lineage tags).
- 2026-03-01: Requested security/data-governance review; flagged PII columns to be tokenized at ingestion.
- 2026-03-02: Started integration tests in staging; discovered a deduplication edge-case for retries — created follow-up subtask ENG-246813 to harden idempotency logic.

Open questions / risks:
- Snowflake concurrency limits during large parallel backfills; mitigation: rate-limit via Airflow pools and use partitioned, incremental backfills.
- Affinity signature interpretability: analysts will need helper UDFs to decode approximate buckets; create a small decoding library in analytics-utils repo.
- Cost visibility: need a cost attribution report for the snapshot S3 stage and Snowflake compute (pending ENG-314159 team assistance).

Reviews & feedback:
- PM Samantha Ortiz: approved schema for dashboard needs, requested additional per-tenant quota columns. Action: add quota columns in next iteration.
- Analytics lead Priya Nair: validated fingerprint approach and suggested sampling-based cardinality checks during nightly compaction.
- Security (requested): must add KMS encryption for snapshot stage and ensure masked tenant PII in exported datasets.

Next actions (owner: Marcus Kwan):
- Unblock staging Snowflake slots with infra (ENG-17789) and re-run integration test matrix (due 2026-03-05).
- Complete security review and update ingestion tokenization to redaction pipeline (due 2026-03-08).
- Run staggered prod backfill for 8->52 weeks based on risk group and validate dashboards (start 2026-03-10).

Acceptance criteria (final):
- tenant_weekly_usage_v1 available in prod schema with documented contract and sampling test coverage
- Dashboard queries for top 10 Console slices show >=5x median improvement and 95th %ile < 800ms
- Backfill completed for baseline tenants and no data parity regressions vs raw facts
- Security sign-off obtained and snapshot stage cryptographically protected

Comments: 
- 2026-02-20 Samantha Ortiz: "Nice trade-off on affinity fingerprinting — keeps cardinality under control while preserving cohort queries. Please add a decode helper for analysts."
- 2026-03-01 Priya Nair: "We should add nightly cardinality telemetry to detect skewed tenants earlier."
- 2026-03-02 Marcus Kwan: "Created ENG-246813 to address idempotency edge cases observed in staging; integration tests in flight."

Notes for future iteration:
- Consider adding an optional per-route micro-rollup table for very heavy tenants (follow-up if skewging continues).
- Evaluate moving fingerprint decoding into a UDF for faster ad-hoc exploration.
